ai.description: *Gegeneophis krishni* is a slender, 16–20 cm caecilian with a uniform dark-brown dorsum and paler venter. It is distinguished by its 115–120 primary annuli and a terminal shield on the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis krishni* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian caecilians by its distinctively pale, whitish-yellow snout that contrasts sharply with its darker body.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis krishni* inhabits moist, shaded soil within tropical evergreen forests and areca nut plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Gurupur caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows to forage for earthworms and small invertebrates in moist soil after rainfall.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis krishni* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in underground nests during the monsoon season. Maternal care involves guarding the eggs until hatching.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis krishni* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it is found at low to mid-elevations in the Wayanad region.
ai.callDescription: The Gurupur Caecilian produces a rhythmic, low-pitched series of clicks or pulses, typically emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter in its subterranean habitat.
